images.title: A chikki piece in fourths
images.purpose: Show that the small chikki piece is 1/4 of the whole because 4 copies of it fill the chikki, and the bigger piece is 3 of those copies, 3/4.
images.composition: One large chikki grid centred in the frame, with labels to its left and right and one short line centred below.
images.exact_structure: One chikki drawn as a grid of 24 equal small squares, 6 across and 4 down. The top left block, 3 across and 2 down, is filled teal #0072B2. The other 18 squares, an L shape, are filled amber #E69F00. Two dashed grey #6B7280 lines, one vertical down the middle and one horizontal across the middle, split the chikki into 4 equal blocks of 3 by 2. Exactly 1 grid, 24 squares, 4 dashed blocks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
small squares of unequal size, or a grid with other than 6 squares across and 4 down
images.takeaway: 4 copies of the small piece fill the chikki, so it is 1/4.
images.description: A 6 by 4 chikki grid split by dashed lines into 4 equal blocks; the teal top left block of 6 squares is 1/4 and the amber L of 18 squares is 3/4.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the dashed blocks the L shape covers and say why it is three fourths.

image_decisions.why: Counting copies of the small piece on the chikki grid is the whole idea, and one grid shows it.
